- **"Business Day"** means any day other than a Saturday, Sunday, or public holiday in the Federal Republic of Nigeria.

- **"Services"** means the preventive and corrective maintenance services described in Article 2.
- **"Term"** means the duration of this Contract as set forth in Article 3.

1.2 **Interpretation.** In this Contract, unless the context otherwise requires: (a) words importing the singular shall include the plural and vice versa; (b) references to "Articles," "Schedules," or "Clauses" are references to articles, schedules, or clauses of this Contract; (c) headings are for convenience only and shall not affect the interpretation of this Contract; (d) references to any statute or regulation include any amendment, re-enactment, or replacement thereof.

---

**ARTICLE 2: SCOPE OF SERVICES**

2.1 **Preventive Maintenance.** The Contractor shall perform preventive maintenance services on the Facilities in accordance with the PM Schedule (Schedule B), which shall include at minimum:

(a) Visual inspection of all PV modules, racking systems, inverters, combiners, and battery enclosures for signs of damage, corrosion, soiling, or loose connections;

(b) Cleaning of PV module surfaces to remove dust, bird droppings, and other debris, using deionized water and soft brushes or squeegees as appropriate;

The Maintenance Contract NDSF-2023, signed by both parties, states its commencement_date as 2023-04-01. Record status: current.

(c) Thermal imaging of electrical connections and components to detect hot spots or abnormal temperature rise;

(d) Verification of inverter operating parameters, including DC input voltage and current, AC output voltage and frequency, and system efficiency;

(e) Inspection and torque-checking of all electrical terminations in combiner boxes, inverters, and battery cabinets;

(f) Testing of battery bank voltage, state of charge, and cell balancing, where applicable;

(g) Functional testing of all safety disconnects, surge protection devices, and grounding systems;

(h) Review and documentation of system performance data from the monitoring platform, including energy yield, availability, and any alarms or fault codes;
**ARTICLE 3: TERM AND COMMENCEMENT**

3.1 **Commencement.** This Contract shall commence on 1 April 2023 (the "Commencement Date"), unless the conditions precedent set out in Clause 3.2 are not satisfied or waived in writing by the Owner on or before such date, in which case the Commencement Date shall be deferred until the date on which all such conditions are satisfied or waived, provided that any such deferral shall not exceed ninety (90) days from the date first stated above, unless otherwise agreed in writing by the Parties.

3.2 **Conditions Precedent.** The obligations of the Contractor under this Contract are subject to the prior satisfaction (or written waiver by the Contractor) of the following conditions:

(a) The Owner shall have delivered to the Contractor a complete and accurate inventory of all equipment and systems comprising the Facilities, including manufacturer serial numbers, model numbers, and commissioning dates;

(b) The Owner shall have provided the Contractor with unrestricted access to the Facilities, including all relevant keys, access codes, and security passes, and shall have confirmed in writing that the site is safe for the Contractor's personnel to enter and perform the Services;

(c) The Owner shall have paid any advance payment due under Article 5 (Payment Terms) in accordance with the terms set out therein; and

(d) The Owner shall have designated a representative (the "Owner's Representative") authorised to give instructions, approve work orders, and receive reports under this Contract, and shall have notified the Contractor in writing of the name and contact details of such representative.

3.3 **Initial Term.** Clause 2.1 of the Maintenance Contract NDSF-2023 specifies an initial_term_months of 24. Record status: current. The initial term of this Contract (the "Initial Term") shall therefore be twenty-four (24) months, commencing on the Commencement Date and expiring at 23:59 on 31 March 2025, unless terminated earlier in accordance with Article 11 (Termination) or extended in accordance with Clause 3.4.

3.5 **Early Termination for Convenience.** The Owner may terminate this Contract for convenience at any time upon giving the Contractor not less than ninety (90) days' prior written notice, in which case the Contractor shall be entitled to payment for all Services performed up to the effective date of termination, plus any reasonable, documented, non-cancellable commitments incurred by the Contractor in anticipation of performing the Services during the notice period.

3.6 **Effect of Expiry or Termination.** Upon expiry or termination of this Contract for any reason:

(a) The Contractor shall deliver to the Owner all data, reports, drawings, and other deliverables prepared under this Contract, along with any equipment, tools, or materials owned by the Owner and in the Contractor's possession;

(b) The Contractor shall remove all its personnel, equipment, and temporary installations from the Facilities within fourteen (14) days, in a manner that does not disrupt the operation of the Facilities;

(c) The Parties shall settle all outstanding invoices and payments within thirty (30) days of the effective date of expiry or termination; and

3.7 **Force Majeure.** Neither Party shall be liable for any delay or failure in performing its obligations under this Contract to the extent that such delay or failure results from a Force Majeure Event, as defined in Article 14 (General Provisions). The Party affected by a Force Majeure Event shall give written notice to the other Party within seven (7) days of the onset of such event, stating the nature of the event, its expected duration, and the steps being taken to mitigate its effects. If a Force Majeure Event continues for more than sixty (60) days, either Party may terminate this Contract by written notice, without liability except for payment for Services performed prior to the effective date of termination.
4.3 **Renewal Notice Requirements.** Any notice of renewal given under Clause 4.2 shall:

(a) be in writing and signed by an authorised representative of the Owner;

(b) state the proposed renewal term, which shall be for a period of twelve (12) months in accordance with Clause 5.3;

(c) be delivered by hand, registered post, or electronic mail to the address specified in Article 16 (Notices); and

(d) be accompanied by a copy of the Owner's most recent board resolution or other evidence of authority to exercise the renewal.

4.4 **Effect of Renewal.** Upon the exercise of the renewal option in accordance with Clauses 4.2 and 4.3, this Contract shall continue in full force and effect for the renewal period on the same terms and conditions, save that:

(b) the annual preventive maintenance (PM) schedule set out in Schedule B shall be updated by mutual agreement of the Parties not less than thirty (30) days before the commencement of the renewal period.

4.5 **Failure to Exercise Renewal.** If the Owner does not give notice of renewal in accordance with Clause 4.2, this Contract shall expire automatically at the end of the then-current term without further notice and without any liability on the part of either Party, except for obligations that have accrued prior to the date of expiry.

**Article 5 — Fees, Payment and Adjustments**

5.2 **Invoicing.** The Contractor shall submit invoices on a monthly basis, no later than the fifth (5th) day of each calendar month for Services performed in the preceding month. Each invoice shall be accompanied by a summary of the work performed, including any corrective maintenance activities, parts replaced, and hours logged.

5.3 **Renewal Option.** The Owner shall have the option to renew this Contract for a further period of twelve (12) months, exercisable in accordance with Clause 4.2. The renewal option shall be available to the Owner at the end of the initial term and, if exercised, shall extend the term of this Contract to 31 March 2026.

6.2 **Adjustment of Service Fee.** The monthly service fee set out in Clause 6.1 shall be reviewed annually on each anniversary of the Commencement Date. Any adjustment shall be calculated based on the percentage change in the National Bureau of Statistics' Producer Price Index for the preceding twelve (12) months, provided that the adjusted fee shall not exceed the previous fee by more than ten percent (10%) in any single review.

6.3 **Mobilisation Fee.** Upon execution of this Contract, the Owner shall pay the Contractor a one-time mobilisation fee of One Million, Two Hundred Thousand Naira (₦1,200,000.00) exclusive of VAT. The mobilisation fee is non-refundable and shall be invoiced within seven (7) days of the Commencement Date.

6.4 **Invoicing.** The Contractor shall submit invoices electronically to the Owner's accounts payable department at the email address specified in Clause 15 (Notices). Each invoice shall reference this Contract number, the relevant billing month, and shall itemise all charges in accordance with the fee structure set out in this Clause 6. The Owner shall not be obliged to pay any invoice that does not comply with this Clause 6.4.

6.5 **Payment Schedule.** Payment of each monthly invoice shall fall due thirty (30) days from the date of receipt of a compliant invoice. The Owner shall make payment by electronic transfer to the Contractor's designated bank account, details of which are set out in Schedule D. Payment shall be deemed made on the date the funds are credited to the Contractor's account.

The Contractor may suspend the provision of Services, in whole or in part, upon fourteen (14) days' written notice to the Owner, if any undisputed invoice remains unpaid for more than sixty (60) days past its due date.

6.7 **Disputed Invoices.** If the Owner disputes any portion of an invoice in good faith, the Owner shall notify the Contractor in writing within fourteen (14) days of receipt of the invoice, specifying the disputed amount and the reasons for the dispute. The Parties shall use reasonable endeavours to resolve the dispute within fourteen (14) days. The undisputed portion of the invoice shall be paid in accordance with Clause 6.5, and the disputed portion shall be paid within thirty (30) days of resolution.

7.1 **Limitation of Liability.** Except as expressly provided in Clauses 7.2, 7.3 and 7.4, and to the maximum extent permitted by applicable law, neither Party shall be liable to the other Party, whether in contract, tort (including negligence), breach of statutory duty, or otherwise, for any: (a) loss of profits; (b) loss of business or business opportunity; (c) loss of anticipated savings; (d) loss of or corruption of data; or (e) any indirect or consequential loss or damage whatsoever, arising under or in connection with this Contract, even if that Party was advised of the possibility of such loss or damage.

5. CONTRACTOR PERFORMANCE SUMMARY – Q2 2024

Mr. Tunde Bakare presented a summary of Helios’ performance for the second quarter of 2024. He noted that overall uptime across the three managed sites (Lagos, Oyo, Kano) averaged 94.7%, slightly below the contractual target of 97%. The shortfall was primarily attributed to the Kano site where inverter failures contributed to extended downtime in May.

Ms. Fatima Bello acknowledged the shortfall and explained that the inverter failures were due to a combination of high ambient temperatures and grid instability in the Kano region. She noted that Helios had deployed additional technical staff to the site in late June and that the situation had improved in July. Mr. Samuel Adeyemi provided a brief overview of the failure log, indicating 14 inverter trips recorded in Q2, of which 11 were resolved within 48 hours.

Mr. Emeka Obi asked whether the performance data had been independently verified. Mr. Bakare confirmed that SunVest’s site supervisors had cross-checked the logs and that the figures were generally accurate, though there remained a discrepancy on one outage event in May (see item 6 below).

6. PROPOSED REVISION TO MAINTENANCE SERVICE FEE – HELIOS PROPOSAL

Mr. Chinedu Okafor presented Helios’ proposal for a revision to the monthly maintenance service fee. He explained that the current contract, signed in January 2023, had a fixed fee of ₦4,500,000 per month for all three sites. Helios was requesting an increase to cover rising diesel costs, labour inflation, and increased frequency of inverter component replacement.

Mr. Emeka Obi asked for the cost analysis to be circulated to SunVest’s finance team for independent review. Mrs. Okafor agreed to send the detailed breakdown to Mrs. Ngozi Eze by Friday, 9 August 2024.

Mrs. Ngozi Eze raised a question about the proposed increase being applied to the base fee or to a revised fee that included the cost of additional services. Mr. Chinedu Okafor clarified that the 12.5% would apply to the current base fee of ₦4,500,000, resulting in a new monthly fee of ₦5,062,500 if approved. He acknowledged that this was a significant increase and expressed willingness to discuss a phased implementation.

Mr. Chinedu Okafor presented the formal proposal (Helios Ref: HE-SV-2024-071) for a 12.5% increase to the monthly maintenance service fee. Key points:
- Current base fee: ₦4,500,000 per month (all three sites)
- Proposed new fee: ₦5,062,500 per month
- Effective date proposed: 1 October 2024

Mr. Chinedu Okafor reiterated that the increase was driven by:
- Diesel cost inflation (average ₦1,250/litre in Q2 2024 vs ₦850/litre in Q1 2023)
- Labour cost adjustments following the new national minimum wage discussions
- Increased frequency of inverter component replacement, particularly at Kano

Mrs. Ngozi Eze asked for the detailed cost breakdown to be sent to her directly. Mr. Chinedu Okafor agreed to forward the full analysis by Friday, 9 August 2024. Mrs. Eze noted that SunVest’s finance team would need at least two weeks to review the figures before any commitment.

3.3 Phased Implementation Discussion
Mrs. Adeola Okafor raised the possibility of a phased implementation rather than a single-step increase. She suggested that Helios might consider:
- Phase 1 (October 2024): 5% increase
- Phase 2 (January 2025): Remaining 7.5% increase

Mr. Chinedu Okafor said he would need to discuss this with Helios’ management. He indicated that a phased approach could be acceptable if SunVest agreed to a longer contract extension (see item 4.0 below). He will revert by 14 August 2024.

3.4 Additional Services – Scope Clarification
Mr. Emeka Obi queried whether the proposed increase covered the additional after-hours callout services that Helios had been providing informally since March 2024. Mr. Chinedu Okafor confirmed that the 12.5% increase did NOT include those additional services. He stated that if SunVest wanted the after-hours callouts to remain included, a separate service level agreement would be required, with an estimated additional cost of ₦350,000 per month. This was noted for further discussion.

4.0 CONTRACT EXTENSION AND NEGOTIATION DEADLINE

Mrs. Adeola Okafor noted that the current contract expires on 31 December 2024. She reminded the meeting that the negotiation must be concluded by 10 September 2024 to allow sufficient time for internal approvals and contract execution before the year-end. This deadline was previously agreed at the 15 July meeting and remains unchanged. Mrs. Adeola Okafor’s negotiation deadline is 10 September 2024 per the meeting minutes, and she requested that all outstanding proposals and counter-proposals be submitted no later than 28 August 2024 to allow for proper review.
